races.name: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On 29th August Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Baila Conmigo
runners_data.note: Lightly tried Flat/hurdles performer with a hurdle win to her name, but her natural closing style means she will be racing in traffic rather than from her preferred rear pitch in this crowded field; sim-going record of 0W0P on similar ground adds concern.

runners_data.name: Hinchinbrooke
runners_data.note: Has placed twice from prominent berths on Standard and achieved a win on similar terms, but in this race his instinct to come from off the pace puts him in the midfield pack where he cannot express his best; 20 days since last run, trainer 0W from 3 recent runners.

runners_data.name: Puppet Master
runners_data.note: Nine runs on Good going with one win and two places; consistent without threatening, and trainer Ciaran Murphy has a live hand in this race with multiple runners — Puppet Master's hold-up style is genuine and the redistribution note is less severe here as he sits in the mapped midfield where he likely belongs anyway.

runners_data.name: Kimi De Mai
runners_data.note: Mullins runner who has found trip and class a challenge lately (0W0P in 2 runs on similar going), but his prominent style is exactly what this uncontested pace shape rewards; Danny Mullins in the saddle is a significant positive and he has run well enough at 16-20f distances to suggest the 2m trip is workable.

runners_data.name: Charles The Bold
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse flagged for fading finishes who has only one run on similar going (finished 9th); mapped to midfield due to the surplus of closers and his fade tendency in the finish makes him a low-probability player in any scenario.

runners_data.name: First Ascent
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott, Jack Kennedy combination gives this prominent racer the tactical edge; four places from eight runs on Good ground and a recent second at 16f on Good make this one of the most credible prominent types in the field behind Le Roi Arthur.

runners_data.name: Grabat
runners_data.note: Two runs, both on Good going, finishing 6th and 11th — limited evidence and a true hold-up style means he is not operating from his natural position in this race shape; Philip Fenton trainer but 0W0P from two recent runners, 36 days since last run.

runners_data.name: Jodoro
runners_data.note: Several runs around this trip on Good going with modest results (0W0P in six runs on similar going); an unconvincing record over hurdles and an unpredictable jumping career (unseated once) makes this a difficult horse to trust in a single-pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Le Roi Arthur
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and the horse who defines the race shape; has placed in a chase at 18f on Good and is lightly tried over hurdles — if he jumps cleanly and bowls along, he is the horse everyone else has to beat and could simply steal this.

runners_data.name: Anns Getaway
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading finishes with two runs on Good going both ending outside the frame; a natural hold-up horse redistributed into midfield means he faces a double difficulty — wrong position and a tendency to weaken late.

runners_data.name: Mistakenforanother
runners_data.note: Four runs on Good ground with a placed effort (2nd at 16f) and a midfield style that is genuinely mapped rather than redistributed; the most credible of the hold-up brigade if the pace does collapse, with Daniel King a capable rider at this level.

runners_data.name: Rene's Gold
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with a fade tendency flagged; one run on similar going finished 8th, which is poor evidence for trust in any scenario; style is unknown (U) and Ross O'Sullivan has one runner from 13 recent starters.

runners_data.name: Rose Mountain
runners_data.note: Four runs on Good, all finishing between 9th and 16th — no encouragement from the form figures, and a fade tendency compounds the lack of pace profile that suits this race shape; very hard to make a case for involvement.

runners_data.name: Really Truly
runners_data.note: J J Slevin rides for a powerful O'Brien yard on a 4yo with one run (11th on Good at 16f); recent run 8 days ago suggests fitness, but the form is weak and the hold-up style means she enters the midfield scrum with no obvious advantage.

runners_data.name: Rickety Kate
runners_data.note: Debutant from Joseph Patrick O'Brien's high-strike yard; no form, going, or style data available — the unknown element could cut either way, but a 17-runner field over jumps is a tough introduction for any newcomer.

runners_data.name: Loadstone
runners_data.note: Another O'Brien newcomer with no public form; the yard's 7/57 fortnight strike rate gives some confidence in preparation, but the absence of any race data means probability of impact is speculative at best.

runners_data.name: Geashill Poet
runners_data.note: Adrian Murray's unknown debutant; the trainer has 1/3 recent runners which is a positive marker at this level, but the lack of form, style, or going data makes assessment impossible beyond the yard angle.

races.paceDynamic: Le Roi Arthur is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner maiden hurdle and, crucially, has no obvious rival willing to press him early on Good ground over 2m at Kilbeggan. With Le Roi Arthur able to dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the front, the race will be run at a measured tempo through the early stages before he kicks on turning for home — a shape that heavily favours prominent racers who can track him without burning fuel. Kimi De Mai and First Ascent are the most likely horses to secure genuine prominent positions and capitalise on the soft, sustainable pace. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear — Hinchinbrooke, Grabat, Charles The Bold, Anns Getaway, and Baila Conmigo are all true closers squeezed into a midfield cluster, meaning those who get off the pace face a genuinely compromised passage unless the front-runner fades sharply. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours horses running prominently, with Le Roi Arthur himself a legitimate each-way threat if he gets it all his own way.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Le Roi Arthur Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Le Roi Arthur bowls along unchallenged and sets a comfortable tempo that suits the leader and those tracking him.
scenarios.body: Le Roi Arthur controls the race from the front without being pressured, and Kimi De Mai or First Ascent slot in directly behind, travelling well throughout; as the tempo quickens from 3 out, the horse(s) with best jumping and fitness inherit the advantage. Prominent racers win here because the lack of early pressure ensures they spend energy at the right time, not wasted chasing a vanishing leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Le Roi Arthur weakens in the final flight and a close-tracking horse collars him on the run-in.
scenarios.body: The sustainable gallop has conserved enough energy in the prominent chasers — First Ascent and Kimi De Mai — that they can surge past a fading leader in the last 100 yards on good ground. First Ascent's form at this trip on Good and Jack Kennedy's positional awareness make him a strong beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Le Roi Arthur sets a faster-than-expected gallop and ties up, opening the door for midfield horses to finish past him.
scenarios.body: A faster early pace would string the field out and create genuine late ground for the hold-up runners, but the majority tagged [REDISTRIBUTED] — including Hinchinbrooke, Grabat, and Baila Conmigo — are squeezed into midfield rather than their natural deep-closing berths, reducing their ability to unleash a true late run. Mistakenforanother, who has shown a placed effort from midfield on Good going, is among the few realistic beneficiaries if this unlikely shape materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexpected Newcomer Impact
scenarios.trigger: If one of the O'Brien-trained unknowns — Rickety Kate, Loadstone, or Geashill Poet — shows raw ability and runs greenly but efficiently into contention.
scenarios.body: With going style and form both unknown, any of these lightly raced debutants could surprise a weak maiden field if they possess natural jumping ability and settle in a decent position; J J Slevin's experience on Really Truly adds another wildcard from the O'Brien yard. The probability is low simply because unknown quantities in a 17-runner field on a flat, uncontested gallop are more likely to be caught out by traffic or inexperience.

watchPoints.text: Le Roi Arthur's jumping — if he makes a significant error at any of the early hurdles, it will disrupt the race shape entirely and release the field from a single-pacer scenario into chaos.

Midfield traffic — with Hinchinbrooke, Grabat, Charles The Bold, Anns Getaway, and Baila Conmigo all funnelling into the same central channel, watch for horses becoming boxed in on the final bend, particularly affecting Mistakenforanother and Hinchinbrooke.

Kimi De Mai's jumping — his hurdles form shows he has struggled at 17-19f and this is his first attempt at 16f; if he fidgets at a hurdle early, Mullins may have to take a pull and lose the prominent ground he needs.

O'Brien debutants (Rickety Kate, Loadstone) — both from a powerful yard with strong recent form; if either is strongly supported in the market pre-race, treat as a serious unknown rather than a filler.

First Ascent's finishing effort — watch whether Jack Kennedy commits early or waits; if he settles two or three off Le Roi Arthur's heels, this horse's Good-ground placed record over this trip becomes very relevant in the straight.

races.name: Follow Kilbeggan On Instagram Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Facile Ocean
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who finished well to win over 16f on good ground 13 days ago; Eoghan Finegan's 5lb claim is a tangible asset, and the step up to 2m3f looks genuinely within range given her 19f placed efforts.|

runners_data.name: Magico
runners_data.note: Well-rated Mullins runner (OR 120) stepping up to a longer trip after 76 days off; his prominent style suits a controlled gallop but he has been beaten in good company before and the layoff is a factor.|

runners_data.name: No Mon No Fun
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on good ground and clearly handles this sort of trip; Jack Doyle's 0/0 in-form trainer is flagged, and the fall and pulled-up entries in recent form mean jumping reliability must be proven before trusting fully.|

runners_data.name: Rosie's Wings
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who controls the race shape; six similar-going runs show she stays and handles good, and Danny Gilligan knows this horse well — her ability to dictate terms unchallenged is the central question of this race.|

runners_data.name: Mino Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy aboard a Gordon Elliott four-year-old rated 123 — top combination in the race; four runs on good ground show consistent prominence and the 2m3f trip is a logical step for a horse who has won over 17f.|

runners_data.name: La Cote Fleurie
runners_data.note: Two wins from three runs on good ground, including over 20f, making her the most obvious course-and-distance profile fit in the race; 85 days off is the only caveat, though De Bromhead horses often need the outing.|

runners_data.name: Eaglewood
runners_data.note: OR 93 with a patchy recent record (9th, 14th in last two), this horse naturally wants to race prominently but is realistically boxed out of that position by the weight of classier prominent types — its chance is diminished by being forced to race in an unfamiliar midfield role.|

runners_data.name: Katie Can't Count
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and entirely unexposed — just one hurdle run on record, a fourth over 19f on good ground; the Mullins yard can produce them fresh, but the lack of data makes this a significant unknown even with Brian Hayes riding.|

runners_data.name: Lakewood Rose
runners_data.note: Amateur rider (7lb claim) on an eight-year-old with OR 98 who has not won in five runs and has repeatedly finished mid-to-rear on good ground over similar trips — hold-up style with little evidence of a meaningful late burst.|

races.paceDynamic: Rosie's Wings is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one genuine pace-setter in a nine-runner field, she should be able to dictate a measured gallop from the front without being pressured into a suicidal tempo. Behind her, Mino Des Mottes, Magico, No Mon No Fun, and La Cote Fleurie all want prominent ground, creating a congested chasing pack where traffic problems between the second-last and last are a genuine risk. This field holds more prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate; of those, Mino Des Mottes (Jack Kennedy, Gordon Elliott) and La Cote Fleurie (Darragh O'Keeffe, De Bromhead) have the class and tactical jockeyship to actually secure their natural position, while Eaglewood — a genuine prominent racer — has been redistributed to midfield because he is realistically unlikely to win the battle for those berths. A controlled, honest gallop on good ground over 2m3f at Kilbeggan is a classically front-runner-friendly scenario, but the prominent congestion means any horse that can travel smoothly in the first four and pick up fluently from the second-last will hold the tactical edge — this race shape favours prominently-ridden horses with a clean jumping record and proven class on good ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rosie's Wings Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rosie's Wings leads unchallenged and sets a genuine but sustainable gallop that strings the field out.
scenarios.body: Rosie's Wings dictates on her own terms and, with the prominent group stretched and bumping into each other, she retains enough in reserve to hold on up the run-in; her good-ground record (1W3P in six similar-going runs) supports this strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Class Asserts
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group settles cleanly behind Rosie's Wings and a well-rated prominent horse picks her off from the second-last.
scenarios.body: With the pace controlled and honest, a prominent horse that jumps fluently and travels within itself will find the track and going ideal to sweep past the leader late; Mino Des Mottes and La Cote Fleurie are the two most likely to execute this given their class and proven jockeys.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fast enough through prominent congestion to set up a strong finish for a hold-up horse coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Facile Ocean has winning form at this trip on good ground and a 5lb-claiming jockey who can find cover, so if the prominent scrimmaging burns enough fuel, she is the most credible late finisher; Lakewood Rose is too exposed at OR 98 to seriously threaten but could complete the frame.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If early jumping errors or prominent pile-ups cause the race to unravel, producing a slowly-run lottery.
scenarios.body: Katie Can't Count is lightly raced and entirely unexposed over hurdles — in a scrambled race she could outclass rivals on raw ability without needing to produce a tactical performance; this scenario is low-probability precisely because there is enough class and experience in the field to keep order.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a traffic incident 2-3 out as Mino Des Mottes, Magico, No Mon No Fun, and La Cote Fleurie all converge on the same prominent berths — any horse trapped wide or sandwiched at a hurdle in that group could lose lengths or fall.|

Rosie's Wings jumping — if she makes a significant error at any of the early hurdles she will surrender her lead and the race shape collapses, removing the controlled pace that her chance depends on entirely.|

La Cote Fleurie's 85-day absence is a watch point; De Bromhead horses often need a run, and if she is not fully tuned a prominent runner left short of fuel from the home turn could stop quickly and cause interference.|

Eaglewood's redistribution to midfield means he will likely be racing against his instincts — watch for him to push forward early before being outgunned, potentially complicating life for Facile Ocean and Lakewood Rose behind him.|

Katie Can't Count is wholly unknown beyond a single fourth-place run — if she moves conspicuously well in the market before the off, a Mullins bounce from obscurity is not impossible in a race lacking a dominant class standout.|

races.name: Tom Lynam Memorial Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cloonainra
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for John McConnell with solid Good-ground form (sim-going 9/15), well-placed on OR 110 at top weight; rider Shane Fitzsimons claims 7lb which partially offsets, and recent form of 7/10/5 suggests consistency without a clean break.|

runners_data.name: Magic Day
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter; De Bromhead's mare has the field to herself up front but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is not relevant here — she IS on the lead — and she must be respected as the race-shaper even if her OR 110 mark is competitive.|

runners_data.name: Mysilverriverfeale
runners_data.note: Won at Killarney on Good (1/19f/GOO) and placed twice more on similar surfaces; Thomas Cooper's five-year-old has a strong sim-going record (6/8), stays 2m3f well and Daniel King rides — a genuine prominent contender at OR 106.|

runners_data.name: Somersby Roost
runners_data.note: True hold-up type for Oliver McKiernan, last seen pulling up twice (PP) but won on Good over this exact trip earlier in the season; 42 days off may have freshened him, and Phillip Enright is an astute pilot if the race is run to suit a closer.|

runners_data.name: Bhean Saibhre
runners_data.note: Five-year-old filly prominent racer, won on Good at 2m2f; Peter Smithers claims 5lb for Aidan Howard but recent form of 4/8/P/2 is patchy — the tongue-tie is retained and she'll need a smooth jumping round to feature from OR 105.|

runners_data.name: Cocovic
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for E McNamara with two seconds on Good at 20f — well-suited by this trip and surface (4/8 sim-going); Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim helps at OR 105, and if the pace is honest he has a realistic late-run profile.|

runners_data.name: Pride Of Place
runners_data.note: Three wins from 10 starts on Good (3W7P sim-going) and a course-type performer over big-field handicap trips; Ed Bolger's veteran is best at 2m5f-plus so this 2m3f is on the sharp side, and a P last time out is a concern despite the Good ground tick.|

runners_data.name: Secret Rock
runners_data.note: Headgear-free, genuine hold-up type who won at 2m on Good 11 days ago — very quick return for Cian Collins; the step up from 16f to 19f suits, but the tight turnaround means fitness is proven while freshness is absent, and he tends to be positional.|

runners_data.name: Emesteraye
runners_data.note: Ross O'Sullivan's five-year-old has three consecutive thirds, all on Good ground at around 16f — consistent but hasn't won and the step up to 19f is uncharted territory; Danny Gilligan has the mount and the tongue-tie is a constant, though the finishing pattern suggests a horse that doesn't quite see the trip out.|

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose best form (3rd at 24f, Good) suggests he wants further; Brian McMahon's gelding has a patchy record in big fields and the 0W from 15 sim-going runs flags a horse who places without winning — OR 103 is workable but needs a slow pace to deliver.|

runners_data.name: Diamond Tipp
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes over on Martin Hassett's six-year-old who placed (2nd) on Good at 18f recently; tongue-tie and pads (tp) headgear retained, and while the Good ground is fine (12/14 sim-going), four non-completions in the last six runs (P,P,?,?) point to jumping fragility in a 19-runner field.|

runners_data.name: The Monkey Pole
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for N Dooly, three placed efforts on Good at around 16-18f but hasn't won from seven sim-going runs; Richard Condon's 5lb claim helps at OR 102 but recent form of 4/P/3 and a tendency to find only one lacking on the run-in limits confidence.|

runners_data.name: Parkgarve
runners_data.note: Won at Roscommon on Good over 18f 12 days ago — a quick return but in form; Ian Donoghue's stable is firing (T14: 2/8) and the horse has strong sim-going figures (13/15); the longer 19f trip here is the only query but the recent form and yard confidence are genuine positives at OR 99.|

runners_data.name: Malikanna
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh rides a true hold-up horse forced into a midfield map position by field congestion — the STYLE_FIT (0.93) discount applies because she won't get her natural rear-of-field berth; best form came over 16f on Good (2nd) and the drop to OR 97 helps, but the positional compromise is a real tactical disadvantage.|

runners_data.name: Blue Reed
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a win at 19f/Good and two seconds on similar surfaces; Cian Collins' sprightly seven-year-old (OR 95, sim-going 8/15) carries tp headgear, Eoghan Finegan claims 5lb, and the trip and ground are squarely in his wheelhouse — an each-way live option at a likely generous price.|

runners_data.name: Solar Generation
runners_data.note: Martin Brassil's five-year-old returns from 98 days off — the longest absence in the field — with only three career runs and a noted tendency to fade in the finish; remapped from hold-up to midfield by redistribution, the STYLE_FIT (0.90) penalty and the layoff mean this is a watch-and-learn run.|

runners_data.name: Kome Dans Un Reve
runners_data.note: Philip Fenton's six-year-old ran just eight days ago (6th, 16f, Good) and fades in finishes — a double concern in a 19-runner staying handicap; running out of his natural hold-up position due to redistribution (STYLE_FIT 0.90), and no jockey declared at time of analysis, this is effectively a field-filler at current evidence.|

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer who cannot secure his preferred position in this crowded field and has been remapped to midfield — Ciaran Murphy's team is in form (T14: 3/13) and the horse has solid sim-going stats (12/15), but the style compromise materially reduces his winning chance; best treated as a place curiosity rather than a win banker.|

runners_data.name: Andyourbirdcansing
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a win on Good at 20f (1W, 14/15 sim-going) but recent form of 5/6/5/1/0 is inconsistent; John Patrick Ryan's runner is a true prominent type squeezed out of position by the field's surplus of pace horses — the STYLE_FIT (0.93) flag tempers enthusiasm, though the distance and ground profile are correct.|

races.paceDynamic: Magic Day is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with Darragh O'Keeffe in the saddle for Henry De Bromhead, is likely to bowl along at a controlled, uncontested gallop over this 2m3f trip on Good ground — a sustainable pace rather than a true test. Behind Magic Day, Cloonainra, Mysilverriverfeale, Bhean Saibhre, Pride Of Place, Blue Reed and Parkgarve all have genuine prominent claims, meaning the race for the first few positions behind the leader will be competitive and likely to produce a tidy, strung-out group rather than a massed cavalry charge. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Steps In The Sand and Andyourbirdcansing are natural prominent racers who will be forced wider in the pack, while Malikanna, Solar Generation and Kome Dans Un Reve are true hold-up horses remapped to midfield — their redistribution is a function of field congestion, not genuine positional flexibility. With one horse setting a measured pace and several prominently-minded types tracking close but unable to pressure, this race shape strongly favours a horse who can travel handily in the leading group and produce a clean, well-timed jump at the last — the patient prominent profile is the winning template here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Day sets an honest but unchallenged gallop and the race is decided by a horse travelling smoothly just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Magic Day dictates from the front at a fair clip on Good ground, with the prominent group — Cloonainra, Mysilverriverfeale, Blue Reed and Parkgarve — travelling in his slipstream through the back straight before one pounces from the second-last hurdle; this shape rewards horses with clean jumping and a reliable jump-and-run finish rather than a deep finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Falters, Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Day sets too slow a tempo early, bunching the field, and a genuine hold-up horse produces a decisive late run.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian early gallop creates a compressed race that turns into a sprint from two out, bringing closers like Cocovic, Diamond Tipp and Somersby Roost into play as the prominent brigade tire; on Good ground over this trip a strong-finishing hold-up type can pick up the pieces if the first two flights are dawdled through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Magic Day Bowls On
scenarios.trigger: If Magic Day is allowed to stride clear and converts his front-running role into an unassailable advantage at a strong clip.
scenarios.body: De Bromhead's mare, uncontested on the front end, effectively controls every variable — jumping fluently, dictating tempo and finding enough in reserve to hold on from the last; the prominent chasers struggle to reel in a horse who has banked energy by jumping cleanly without rival pressure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Race, Midfield Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely and the redistributed prominent types cause interference or early crowding, producing a messy, falsely-run contest.
scenarios.body: Congestion among the prominent group disrupts rhythm and hands an advantage to a horse who settles in mid-division and arrives fresh at the business end; Steps In The Sand or Andyourbirdcansing, if they find clear air having been unable to claim their natural position, could benefit from a chaotic unfolding but their style-fit discount tempers confidence in this shape delivering.

watchPoints.text: Magic Day's uncontested lead is the fulcrum of the whole race — watch whether Darragh O'Keeffe elects to inject pace from the second fence or dawdles, because the tempo she sets will determine whether closers or chasers dominate.|

Parkgarve returned a winner just 12 days ago and Ian Donoghue's yard is striking at 25% over 14 days — a second quick-turnaround run in form from an OR of 99 makes this horse a pace-shape beneficiary worth tracking from the front.|

Diamond Tipp goes with Jack Kennedy but has failed to complete in multiple recent starts — in a 19-runner field on a circuit track, a jumping error from this horse could cause serious interference for the prominent group behind Magic Day.|

Blue Reed (OR 95) holds solid form at this trip and going profile but will be unfancied in the market; if Magic Day sets an honest gallop and the prominent group races cleanly, this horse's course-type profile could deliver value beyond its expected price.|

races.name: New Forest Estate & Golf Club Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: One Way Traffic
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a sound Good-ground record (sim-going 6/15, one win one place) trained by Oliver McKiernan who sends horses fit; the 17-day turnaround is sharp, and the 3m2f trip is well within range for this 9-year-old who placed over similar distances on Good.|

runners_data.name: Gorthill
runners_data.note: Front-runner with the best sim-going profile in the race (9/10 Good-ground runs, 1W3P) and the trip suits a staying chaser at OR=97; amateur claim (7lb) from Mr S Connor helps the weight, and the 19-day break is routine for Stephen Carlin.|

runners_data.name: Lecale's Diamond
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse flagged for fading finishes, but the sole win came on Good and the 35-day rest may have freshened a 6-year-old who has been busy; Gavin Cromwell's 7/20 trainer strike-rate in 14 days is noteworthy, and the Good ground suits (sim-going 6/9).|

runners_data.name: Broken Ice
runners_data.note: True hold-up type with a tight 6-day turnaround that must be noted — John McConnell runs horses quickly when fit, and the form figure of 3 over 24f on Good is the strongest recent evidence here; however, sim-going numbers (12/15) are modest and the OR=93 represents a class ceiling.|

runners_data.name: Sampoet
runners_data.note: Front-runner by style with tongue-strap and pads, but recent form (584U7U) is deeply unconvincing and sim-going is poor at 13/15; will press Gorthill early and likely fade, but his role is to create pressure rather than win — D M Christie sends him fit enough to do that job.|

runners_data.name: Our Zebo
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with an exceptional Good-ground record at this distance (3W7P in 15 sim-going runs) who has not raced for 336 days — the long absence is the one significant concern, but Noel Kelly's 1/10 recent trainer rate suggests confidence; if fit, this profile suits the race shape ideally.|

runners_data.name: Zolpharine
runners_data.note: A genuine closer in form (two recent wins on Good, OR=89 and climbing) whose natural habitat is the rear of the field — placed into midfield on this map because the hold-up berths are oversubscribed, which means it may not get the clean run from the back it prefers; STYLE_FIT of 0.92 tempers confidence despite the strong recent record.|

runners_data.name: Glendine Billy
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes the ride for Anthony Mullins, which is always worth noting, but the form string (0P9-84) is weak and this horse's natural closing style is compromised by the crowded back-markers scenario; sim-going of 11/15 confirms Good ground is not a concern, but the position problem is real.|

runners_data.name: Joe's Turn
runners_data.note: Two wins and four places in 15 Good-ground runs (sim-going 11/15) point to a consistent type who thrives on this surface over staying trips, but the 40-day break and age (10) add uncertainty; the horse's true style is hold-up, forced into midfield here, so its best chance depends on the pace collapsing in the final mile.|

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent form (421321) with two wins and four places in five Good-ground runs — the best recent hit-rate in the field — yet at OR=81 and age 13 the class ceiling is genuine; in-form and fresh off 7 days, this horse's natural style is late-running but it may find a rhythm slightly further forward than its true preference given the map displacement.|

runners_data.name: Seventy Eight Team
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Paul John Gilligan whose form (45P-P8) lacks the finishing positions to inspire confidence, but the style suits if the pace is hot and the field strings out; sim-going of 11/15 is respectable and the 21-day break is standard.|

runners_data.name: Deadheat
runners_data.note: At 13 years old with a recent form figure of 0 and sim-going of just 4/15, the evidence is firmly against this horse on Good ground; a genuine closer in style, it finds itself unable to access its natural deep-lying position in this field, which compounds an already difficult profile.|

runners_data.name: He Fitz In
runners_data.note: Long absent (197 days) and wearing a visor, with six consecutive finishing positions in the 6-7 range — consistency of mediocrity on a horse that has never threatened on Good ground (sim-going 9/15); the redistribution to midfield from its natural hold-up role is an additional complication rather than a benefit.|

runners_data.name: Tullabrack Lad
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading finishes and off 131 days, this 7-year-old has a clean Good-ground blank (0W0P in sim-going) and has yet to prove stamina for 3m2f; the Style_FIT of 0.90 — the lowest in the field — reflects how poorly the forced midfield position aligns with its natural late-running preference.|

races.paceDynamic: Gorthill and Sampoet are the two confirmed front-runners in a 14-horse field over 3m2f at Kilbeggan on Good ground, and both are expected to press from the outset, meaning this race will be run at an honest, sustained gallop from flag to finish with no tactical dawdling. Gorthill has strong Good-ground form and a record of racing prominently across trips, while Sampoet has headgear (tongue-strap/pads) and a history of front-running even if his recent form figures are modest — together they guarantee early pressure that will be maintained into the back straight and beyond. Seventy Eight Team from the prominent position will likely sit just behind the two leaders, keeping the tempo honest through the middle stages, meaning the race is unlikely to bunch up or produce a false pace. With a field this deep in hold-up horses, the redistribution note is important: Zolpharine, Glendine Billy, Joe's Turn, Fr Gilligansvoyge, Deadheat, He Fitz In, and Tullabrack Lad are all genuine closers mapped to midfield because the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear — in reality, those with the sharpest handlers or widest draws will get closer to the rear than others, but the prominent berths will be controlled by Gorthill, Sampoet and Seventy Eight Team. This race shape — honest early gallop, two genuine pace-setters, Good ground and a stiff 3m2f trip — strongly favours patient, well-staying hold-up types who can travel through the field without burning fuel early and pick off a tiring leader in the final two fences.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Gorthill and Sampoet set a genuine searching pace that strings the field out and softens the leaders by the final mile
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other up over the demanding trip, leaving the race wide open to hold-up horses tracking through on Good ground in the closing stages; genuine stayers with sound jumping and good sim-going records at this distance are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Sampoet or Gorthill is allowed to dictate a controlled rhythm and their rival drops away before the pressure mounts
scenarios.body: One of the two leaders finds the other crying enough before the final circuit, effectively converting a contested lead into a solo display; Gorthill's strong Good-ground profile (1W3P in 10 Good-ground runs) gives him the better credentials to be that horse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Picks Up Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but collapses at the second-last fence, allowing a prominent-to-midfield tracker to pounce close home
scenarios.body: Seventy Eight Team or Our Zebo, racing just off the pace and conserving energy, creep into contention as the front-runners tire over the final three fences; Our Zebo's excellent Good-ground record at Kilbeggan-style tracks and win at OR=90 gives him a credible profile here despite the long absence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail to Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves more controlled than anticipated and hold-up horses are left with too much to do on the run-in
scenarios.body: Several redistribution horses — Glendine Billy, Deadheat, He Fitz In — are unable to find their true deep-closing position and are caught in no man's land through the race, finishing out of the placings; the winner comes from the prominent group with enough class to sit handily without overexerting.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Gorthill or Sampoet is allowed to stride clear into the first fence — if one jumps ahead by two lengths, the other may not be able to sustain the pressure across 3m2f and will drop away by the back straight, changing the complexion of the race entirely.

Our Zebo returns from 336 days off; watch the paddock closely for signs of condition — if the horse looks sharp and well-muscled, the Good-ground record (3W7P) makes it one of the most dangerous in the field regardless of the layoff.

Fr Gilligansvoyge's age (13) and consistent recent form (421321) are in direct tension — watch whether this horse is travelling fluently at the fourth-last fence, because if it is still going well there its pattern suggests it will finish in the frame.

Zolpharine has won two of its last three starts on Good ground but is a genuine hold-up horse compressed into midfield by the pace map; watch how Daniel King positions it in the early stages — if he drops out wide and to the rear regardless, the horse is in better shape than the map suggests.

With 14 runners over fences in a 3m2f handicap, watch the first fence for any scrimmaging — Broken Ice's 6-day turnaround and He Fitz In's 197-day absence mean those two in particular could be unpredictable at the early obstacles.

races.name: Belvedere House & Gardens Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Charlie Luciano
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Noel Meade ridden by 7lb claimer Mr D McGill, who will need a clear run late over 3m2f; won over 26f on Good 21 days ago which is an encouraging recent form line, and 14 of 15 comparable-going runs show competitive returns, but from this style his chance depends entirely on the pace being strong enough to bring him into play.

runners_data.name: A Wave Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up type returning after 67 days off for J P Broderick, which is the primary concern here; has placed on Good at 20-21f multiple times but this 3m2f trip is at the outer edge of what his recent form suggests he stays, and the layoff makes his fitness for a strong stamina test speculative.

runners_data.name: Ceanndana
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a sound record on Good ground for Ross O'Sullivan, wearing a hood (hg:p) which has featured in recent runs; only 13 days since last run and returned a five-length effort on similar ground recently, giving Keith Donoghue a live hold on the pace — the consistent placed form across 20-24f trips makes this a natural fit for the race shape.

runners_data.name: Koori Star
runners_data.note: The confirmed front runner and likely pace-setter for Peter Fahey, but the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 signals this horse is effectively racing out of its most productive role; recent form of 4-5-6-8-9 is a declining sequence and the sim-going record of just 8/15 is modest — sets the tempo but is not the one to trust to maintain it to the finish.

runners_data.name: Ira Hayes
runners_data.note: Prominent type wearing visor (hg:v) for John McConnell who has posted 3 winners from 28 runners over the last 14 days — a strong in-form angle; won over 22f on Good and ran second over 24f on Good, suggesting both the trip and conditions suit, and 19 days since last run keeps freshness in reserve for a 3m2f test.

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Six-year-old prominent racer wearing a tongue tie (hg:t) for Gordon Elliott with Jack Kennedy aboard, combining the best jockey-trainer combination in the field; consistent placed record (2-2-3-3-4-2 recently) over trips up to 26f on Good ground — steps up in distance here but the profile of a young stayer with scope to improve makes this a compelling prominent contender.

runners_data.name: Granville Street
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Ciaran Murphy whose recent trip distances cluster around 12-14f, making this 3m2f test a significant distance stretch; while he ran fourth over 22f on Good 20 days ago, the bulk of his history is over much shorter and the sim-going record of just 7/15 is the weakest in the field — difficult to see how his late run unfolds over this trip.

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good for John Patrick Ryan with J J Slevin, a high-class jockey booking that commands respect; however, this horse is a true hold-up operator pushed into a midfield map position because the rear of the field is congested — his natural finishing kick is partially neutralised by the compressed race shape, and the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 reflects that reality.

runners_data.name: The Dara Man
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old hold-up horse wearing a tongue tie for the same Ryan yard, with a recent form string containing three non-completions (P, P, F) from his last five starts; like stablemate Ad Caelum he is a genuine rear-of-field type shown in midfield because the redistribution forces him forward — the age, jumping concerns, and style displacement combine to make him the riskiest profile in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Koori Star is the only confirmed front runner in this nine-runner field over 3m2f at Kilbeggan on Good ground, and with just one horse intent on leading, the pace is expected to be honest but controlled rather than truly searching — Koori Star can dictate without significant early pressure and is likely to set a rhythm that suits resolute staying types over prominent racers who need a genuine test. Ceanndana, Ira Hayes, and Scalpnagoon will all want to race prominently and will track Koori Star closely, creating a compact early order that risks turning the contest into a stamina grind from three fences out. With the hold-up brigade unable to dominate from the rear — Ad Caelum and The Dara Man are redistributed to midfield because the field contains more true come-from-behind types than the map can place at the back — the race shape effectively compresses, with little genuine late running room unless the pace collapses. This structure most rewards horses racing prominently with proven stamina and a turn of foot in the final mile, particularly those who can track the leader without burning petrol and pounce when Koori Star's control weakens late. The field holds more hold-up types than can secure a genuine rear position; Ad Caelum and The Dara Man are the most likely to find themselves closer to the action than their natural style dictates, making their finishing kicks less potent.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Koori Star Controls, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Koori Star leads at a sustainable gallop and the prominent trackers ration their energy, the race becomes a stamina test decided in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Ceanndana and Scalpnagoon, racing just off the pace, are best placed to challenge as Koori Star's control fades approaching the last two fences; both carry consistent form on Good ground and have the jumping fluency to capitalise from a prominent pitch.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Collide Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ceanndana, Ira Hayes, and Scalpnagoon all push for position early and the pace quickens beyond Koori Star's comfort, the race becomes a true test of class and fitness.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested gallop from the front filters out the less well-handicapped, and a horse like Ira Hayes — fit under a strong T14 record of 3/28 — who can settle just off a hot pace and pick up stylishly has the profile to thrive; Scalpnagoon's consistent placing record also suits a race where attrition removes rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the front group tie each other up badly, a hold-up horse with a clear run from the final fence could mop up.
scenarios.body: Charlie Luciano showed a win on Good over an equivalent trip in his recent history and Keith Donoghue's partner Ceanndana aside, Charlie Luciano on a clear passage is the most credible beneficiary; A Wave Of The Sea, however, has not run for 67 days and the confidence here is tempered.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Redistribution Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fences cause jumping errors mid-race and the field fractures, a race of attrition with a compressed finish favours whoever has jumped cleanly throughout.
scenarios.body: Ad Caelum, though mapped to midfield and racing somewhat out of his natural hold-up role, has a win over 24f on Good to his name and could capitalise on a depleted finishing field; The Dara Man, aged 11 with recent falls and refusals, is a greater risk than a reward in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Scalpnagoon is the live danger — Jack Kennedy's booking for Gordon Elliott on a six-year-old with relentless placed form and stamina scope is a significant upgrade, and if he travels prominently he could produce more than his OR=112 suggests.

Ira Hayes pairs a fitting visor, a strong trainer-form angle (3/28 in 14 days), and proven form on Good at this trip — watch whether Kenneally (5lb) can park him just off Koori Star without burning out through the final mile.

Koori Star's declining form sequence (9-6-8-5-4 reversed) and the STYLE_FIT flag suggest this horse may not be capable of sustaining the lead it is likely to create — watch for a sudden capitulation from three fences out that brings the race to the prominent trackers.

The Dara Man's jumping record (fall and two pull-ups in five runs) at a course like Kilbeggan with tight fences is a material safety concern for the integrity of the race — any jumping incident from him could affect the following pack.

Ad Caelum's Slevin booking is worth monitoring through the early stages — if Slevin elects to push forward rather than accept a midfield pitch, the horse may actually run closer to its natural style than the map suggests, marginally improving its finishing chance.

races.name: John Thomas McNamara Series Flat Race

runners_data.name: Bellahill
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 6yo for S R B Crawford, last seen 509 days ago, style entirely unknown — the lengthy absence and total absence of handicap or going profile make this a near-impossible runner to map; cannot be trusted at this stage without recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Blackwood Joe
runners_data.note: 5yo for E Sheehy who recorded a fade finish in his only run 18 days ago over today's trip on Good, so the combination of a confirmed stamina concern and a busy schedule raises questions about whether he can sustain his effort in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: In Around Thehouse
runners_data.note: 467-day absentee for S Curling with a fall on his form string, making his physical condition and confidence heading into this race unknowns; style is unclassified and the extended absence means almost everything about his current level is guesswork.

runners_data.name: Long Story
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for John Neilan whose last three runs all produced midfield finishes (7-7-9) on Good ground identical to today — consistent but without a win or place to his name, he fits a scenario where a pace collapse is required rather than a sustainable gallop.

runners_data.name: Ddakji
runners_data.note: Conor Houlihan's 4yo is a genuine hold-up horse placed in midfield on this map because the field is dense with closers; his two runs on Good ground both resulted in tail-end finishes with a fade, so he needs a strong pace he is unlikely to get here, and the style-fit discount (0.90) is merited.

runners_data.name: Hill Silver
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy's 4yo (T14: 3/13, active yard) has shown consistency placing 4th twice on Good ground and is another true hold-up type assigned to midfield by necessity rather than by preference; the redistribution means he is racing outside his comfort zone and the style-fit discount (0.90) applies — look at the trainer's recent strike rate as the primary positive angle.

runners_data.name: Lone Ash Lad
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed 4yo for Noel C Kelly with no last-run data, no form string, and unknown going preference — a genuine wildcard who could sit anywhere in the field and whose chance is entirely speculative.

runners_data.name: Reafadda
runners_data.note: John Patrick Ryan's 4yo has one bumper start behind him (6th, Good ground, 2m) and no wins or places to speak of; hold-up style in a race unlikely to produce a strong enough gallop to facilitate a late rattle through the field is a concern.

runners_data.name: A Quest For Cognac
runners_data.note: Barry John Walsh's 6yo carries a fade warning and has fallen or finished well beaten in recent starts including a 14th on identical Good ground — he is a prominent type who will seek to travel close to Baymount but has shown an inability to sustain that effort, and the headgear note (h) is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Baymount
runners_data.note: Anthony Mullins' 5yo is the lone confirmed front-runner and carries a STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) because while he maps naturally to lead, his wider form (including pulled-up efforts) shows he is not invincible in this role; returning just 14 days after his last run and with one placing on comparable Good ground, his ability to control and then quicken is the central question.

runners_data.name: No Brainer
runners_data.note: P F McEnery's 5yo carries a fade warning, has been pulled up twice recently (P-P0 form), and wears a tongue-strap; even his one comparable run on Good ground (15th) gives no encouragement, and his hold-up style in a race with a compressed pace makes him reliant on conditions that will not materialise.

races.paceDynamic: Baymount is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner bumper field and, with no other genuine pace-setters to press him, he is likely to dictate at a comfortable, controlled gallop over Kilbeggan's flat 2m on Good ground. A Quest For Cognac is the only other prominent-profile runner but carries a fade warning and a poor recent form line, meaning Baymount can coast into a rhythm without being harassed through the early and middle stages. The resulting shape is a steady-to-moderate tempo that compresses the field, shortening the advantage of true hold-up runners and rewarding those who can travel close to the pace and produce a sustained run from 3f out rather than a single explosive burst late. This race shape most strongly favours prominent or mid-division horses who travel smoothly and stay on genuinely, as the lack of strong pace means closers will need to start their move earlier than usual — the field holds more hold-up types than can operate naturally at the rear, with Hill Silver and Ddakji both genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because multiple true closers cannot all find their preferred ground; Baymount and A Quest For Cognac are most likely to actually secure the prominent positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Baymount Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Baymount bowls along at a comfortable clip and no challenger applies pressure through the middle mile.
scenarios.body: Baymount settles into an uncontested lead on Good ground and simply has to maintain his rhythm, with the moderate tempo suiting a horse who can be ridden handily and quicken modestly off a slow pace; the lack of a genuine pace battle means his stamina is rarely tested. Prominent horses who travel close to him early have first use of the gaps and can pick him off if he weakens, but any horse who gets into a good rhythm near the front is the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a mid-division or prominent horse travels smoothly just off the slow pace and times a run perfectly from 2f out.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop set by Baymount means the race is not truly run to suit a genuine hold-up horse, so the winner is most likely a runner who has travelled close enough to pounce rather than one who needs a strong pace to make up lengths; Hill Silver and Ddakji are mapped to midfield but are true hold-up types, meaning their realistic winning chance here depends on moving earlier than natural. A horse with a smooth cruising action that can quicken off a slow pace into the straight takes this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Baymount weakens sharply turning in after controlling throughout and opens the race up for a fresher rival.
scenarios.body: Should the front-runner over-extend early or find the mile mark comes too soon, a horse who has been covered up in midfield and saved ground around the tight Kilbeggan bends could arrive with a decisive run; this is the one scenario where the redistributed hold-up horses' true style pays off, as a collapse of the lead horse creates exactly the late gap they need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses press Baymount unexpectedly early and the race turns messy with no clear front-running order.
scenarios.body: An unusually competitive early phase could see several lightly-raced unknown-style runners throw the race into confusion, producing a stop-start gallop that suits a horse yet to reveal its true profile; lightly-raced types with unexposed form such as Lone Ash Lad or Bellahill could benefit from an unpredictable tempo with unknown quantities across the field.

watchPoints.text: Baymount's early pace-setting will shape the entire race — watch if any runner breaks sharply to press him in the first half-mile, as any unexpected pressure on the leader could significantly change the tempo and blow the dominant scenario apart.

Hill Silver and Ddakji are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield by necessity; watch if their jockeys attempt to push forward early to counteract the redistribution, as a crowded prominent group would change the race shape materially.

A Quest For Cognac has a confirmed fade pattern and is the only other prominent-type runner — if he cracks before the straight, Baymount faces no serious challenge from a handy position, strengthening the lone-leader scenario significantly.

Several runners (Bellahill, In Around Thehouse, Lone Ash Lad) are returning from very long absences or have no form data — watch the market moves for these unknown quantities in the final 30 minutes before the off, as stable confidence would be the only reliable guide.

No Brainer carries a tongue-strap and has two recent pull-ups; watch in-running for any signs of distress or his jockey easing him, which would reduce field interference and tighten the effective contest further.
